utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody this afternoon. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And could we have the appearances, please, for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Kyle Wood, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, learned friends from the OTP, to everybody in the courtroom and around the courtroom. Appearing for the Defence, Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson, with assistants Lejla Gluhic and Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me just mention the very obvious, that for reasons beyond our control, Judge Lattanzi is not here today, so we -- this session will take place pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Sir, good afternoon to you too. Yesterday before you commenced your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Excuse me. I remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth. Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Jusic. Yesterday we stopped while discussing the siege of Sarajevo and very poor flow of information from the field to Sarajevo. You may remember that you said that for a year you did not receive -- or you had no contact with your superior command in Sarajevo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours and everybody present, Madam Vidovic. Yes, I do remember. This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that was the reason for in April or May 1993 for the establishment of a forward command post of the command of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it would be correct to conclude that the headquarters of the Supreme Command during 1992 and the first half of 1993 did not control the situation out in the field outside of Sarajevo, that is.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do think that they did not control the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You remember that you gave testimony to the investigators in September and October 2006 -- correction, 2006. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did provide a statement in September/October last year, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion - and I quote paragraph 71 of your statement to the OTP's investigators, and then there you state that: "Until 1995, the headquarters of the Supreme Command was an imaginary command of the army." First of all, do you remember giving such a statement?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would I be correct in concluding that the reason for your providing such an estimate of the situation -- I correct myself for giving such a statement -- was the fact that the Supreme Command Staff did not control the situation out of -- outside of Sarajevo until 1995?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the reason for me thinking that and maintaining that opinion even today, because this was so, because the Supreme Command Staff had no influence whatsoever on the course of combat operations, defence, and all other military matters that obtained outside of Sarajevo. Corps command was in charge of those matters or brigade commands respectively.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Among other things, this was the reason for a decision to be made on dislocating major parts of the Supreme Command Staff from Sarajevo to the free liberated territory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I presume that this was so. This is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Most of the Supreme Command Staff was located at Kakanj, to your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time I had no direct contacts with the organs of Supreme Command Staff at Zenica, of the forward command post in Zenica, but I do know that some organs of the General Staff were there, deputy commander, operative organ or part of the operative organ, and some other officers from the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusic, maybe we did not understand each other. I would like you to see a document, and then I will ask you questions about it. Currently I'm talking about the Kakanj command post, but I'd like you to take a look at Exhibit 280, if we have it appear on the screen for the witness, please. For the record, this is an order of the Supreme Command Staff of the armed forces dated the 2nd of January, 1994. This is an order for the relocation of the Supreme Command Staff to the command post of Kakanj. Please, Mr. Witness, could you take a look at this document, the first page of this document. Take a look at the introductory part, and then the sentence immediately below the word "order" -- "I order." I'd like to ask you: Did you know that on the 5th of January, 1994, it was ordered for the Supreme Command Staff to relocate to a new command post at Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not learn of this order, but I know it was implemented. The headquarters of the Supreme Command Staff entered certain facilities at Kakanj and established a command post. We called it an IKM or forward command post. I did not see this order, but I knew of its existence. I know it was implemented at -- I visited personally that. That was the headquarters of the General Staff headed by the chief of staff, General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like you to take a look at the last or third page of this document. You mentioned General Hadzihasanovic. You see the signature there on the page. Could you please, being a trained and educated professional soldier, do you agree that in the absence of -- of the commander, his deputy had powers to represent him and to deputise for him?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was the procedure. This was so. I would like to emphasise that at any rate, the deputy commander, and when they were abandoned, then chief of staffs were empowered to regulate certain matters, to organise the work of the command, and the staff as -- as per their job description, and they could make arrangements orally with the command -- they could sign documents. But this was signed by General Hadzihasanovic. I know that -- I knew him because from March to November I was part of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean that they made oral arrangements about powers?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm -- no, I think that they orally arranged about the transfer of the command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I want to make it clear when you said "made oral arrangements," what it really meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if -- I would like this document to be removed from the screen, and I would like the witness to see Exhibit 281.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a look at this document, Witness. It is entitled -- or in other words, this is a Supreme Command Staff document dated 16th February, 1994, and it's entitled "Order, organising the deployment of the Supreme Command of the armed forces." Witness, you just mentioned something that I believe -- what I believe would be very useful. You mentioned the staff of the army. Could you for the benefit of the Trial Chamber explain the following: It is true, isn't it not, that the staff of the army is not the same as Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had analgous formations of the commands and the General Staff. The General Staff comprised of a part of departments and sectors headed by assistant commanders, intelligence, security, morale, finance, logistics, who were not part of the staff and the staff was a separate organisational unit of the General Staff, which in its remit had and in its company -- position had operational centre, operational organ, aspects -- now, just aspects of the forces; such as artillery, communications, engineers, anti-aircraft defence, anti-biological and chemical and nuclear, and IT, informatics. And they had a unit for the supply of the commands. They provided logistics for the command, they supplied materiel, consumable, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness, for such an exhaustive explanation. Let me ask you just one thing: Did I get it right that the staff of the army is an operational arm of the Supreme Command Staff which is in charge of preparing, organising, and monitoring the combat operations? Did I get it right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct in essence, but the Supreme Command Staff or Supreme Command should be understood as the General Staff. The General Staff used to change its title like General Staff, Supreme Command, et cetera, et cetera. So don't think that the -- the staff was the operational organ of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was part of the General Staff. The army staff was a planning organ of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Supreme Command Staff or General Staff.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, take another look at this order, please. Do you agree that the army staff, that operational body of the Supreme Command Staff, was that dislocated to Kakanj? Take a look under "1."

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see very well what is on the document, but I know that this was so. It was dislocated to Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if it is necessary, I may provide you with a paper copy or a hard copy of that order.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what did happen in real life. I don't need this document. I can't see it very clearly on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like the witness to see this hard copy, just in case.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at item number 1, please. Please keep this paper and take a look at item 3. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have page 2 appear on the screen both in the B/C/S and English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please take a look at item number 3. Do you agree that this item regulates that the activities of the staff will be -- proceed in accordance with the staff plan under the direct command of the chief of staff? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is as per procedure; although, it was unnecessary to put it in writing, because it is well known that the chief of staff is in charge of those things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we close this document. Now I'm going to ask you, witness, about some things that you testified to yesterday and which were related to the planning of combat operations. We saw that the staff of the army was dislocated to Kakanj, and you said that as per usual course of proceedings, that staff would be in charge of planning. But, Mr. Jusic, you will agree with me, will you not, that the staff -- Supreme Command Staff, neither that in Sarajevo nor the command post in Kakanj, planned the combat activities at -- around Vozuca Dzep in the July of 1995. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're correct, sir. They did not plan division commands of the 35th Division -- did the planning, corps command did not do the planning either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, that operation in July 1995 against the Vozuca pocket was planned by the command of the 35th Division; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Jusic, what is correct, though, is that the Supreme Command Staff at the beginning of 1995 adopted a directive which concerned the combat activities and operations in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know of it. I extracted tasks for my corps from it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we can have the witness take a look at document D399. It is an act of the army General Staff dated 5th of January, 1995 generated at Kakanj, which is entitled "The directive for continued offensive combat operations." Your Honours, I wanted this document to be translated. It's a lengthy document, and I see it is a very important document and I will say that we will insist on it being translated in its entirety. Unfortunately, the translation service has not managed to translate even the small excerpts that we sought to be translated as a priority, and I will seek your understanding, because this is beyond my powers. The witness, if need be, will be given the copy that I have in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you take a look at this document and confirm whether this is the directive dated 5th of January, 1995, that you had occasion to peruse. Take a look at it. Do you recall this directive it can be seen that is addressed to the commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th Corps and the in accordance with the IBOG.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that the 3rd Corps tasks were listed there and I can remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will come to that. But, first of all, I'd like you to take a look at page 9. And then we will go back to the beginning of this document. Could you scroll down to the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we need from this page, Your Honours, is to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that the brigade general, Hadzihasanovic, produced this document and that it was approved by General Delic?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, if we can take a look at page 10, the one following this one, and then later on I'll be going back to the beginning. If we could take a look. And, Your Honours, I apologise for this part not being translated. I will try to translate it with the help of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, do you agree that it is written here that this directive was made in eight copies and delivered to the commands of seven corps? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature of your commander?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, and do you agree that there's a note that -- to the effect that at a joint meeting in Zenica with the commander of the General Staff, army general Mr. Rasim Delic, on the 25th of December, 1994, partly and orally, this content of this directive has been made known to the chiefs of administrations of the General Staff commanders of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 7th Corps, and deputy commander of the RV commander of GLLC, commandant of guards brigades, assistant commander for aspects of the armed forces, PK for prospective development of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? This is the original, and it says: "Original at the staff of army of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that this directive has been forwarded to all corps.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was definitely received by the 3rd Corps and it can be seen here that all the other corps received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we now please show page 6 of this document. This is page 2 in the English. Page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, look closely at the portion that says "I hereby decide," or "I have decided." I will quote this short portion for you. It reads: "In the coming defensive combat operations, firmly hold the taken line of defence. Continue carrying out offensive combat operations of operative and tactical importance, particularly for the army, with the following objective: Free the PZT --" And this is what I mean to ask you: "PZT" is short for what?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Temporarily occupied territory. Temporarily occupied territory. PZT.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. "Lift the blockade of the surrounding free territories in the Drina River Valley. Lift the siege of Sarajevo. Link up the forces of the 4th and 7th Corps with those of the 5th Corps. Cut off important roads used by the aggressors for supplies and evacuation. Take control of important roads and industrial facilities for our own needs. And create conditions for the final liberation of our homeland. Carry out battles and operations in accordance with the tasks received or authorised by the commander of the BH army General Staff commander." All right. My question about this is as follows: This assignment may be received by the commander, but it can also be approved. And that's not the same, is it?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes., it's not the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Chamber what that means.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The task or an assignment received is a task that a superior command hands out to a subordinate unit. A task that is approved or authorised is a task designed and prepared by a subordinate unit. For this task they seek authorisation or approval from their superior command. This task received is a task planned, a design by a superior command. A task that is approved is something that is designed or planned by the directly subordinate command through whichever command is issuing authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the subordinate command was planning and the commander was authorising this; right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what I said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Can we now please go to page 7 of the Bosnian. The English reference is page 3. Page 7, please. Page 3 in English. Can you please look at items 5 and 6, sir. In actual fact, item 5 is in reference to the tasks of the 2nd Corps and item 6 in relation to the tasks of the 3rd Corps. You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a while ago yourself: "I will know as soon as I set eyes on the tasks that we received at the time. I will be able to recognise them." First of all, let me read out the relevant portion to you, the portion that talks about the tasks of the 2nd Corps. That's 5.2. The task of the 2nd Corps is the following: "Liberate the areas of Mount Majovica [phoen], Ban Brdo, Stolica, Busija, and then a list of locations, and reach the Prevoj-Lopare-Celic road, as well as the following, in coordination with the 3rd Corps, liberate the general sector of Vozuca along the Klokotnica-Sevarlije axis cutting off the Chetnik forces at Mount Ozren. With the assistance of other corps, lift the blockade of the free territories of Srebrenica and Zepa and get as far as the River Drina from Zepa to Zvornik. Use parts of its forces in accordance with the decision of the General Staff and join the effort to lift the siege of Sarajevo." And now on to the task for the 3rd Corps. It reads: "Liberate the general sector of Teslic, reach the Mladikovina-Rankovici-Ukunica [phoen] axis and press on towards Prnjavor. In coordination with the 2nd Corps, clear the general sector of Vozuca along the Sevarlije-Preslica axis, cut off the Chetnik forces at Mount Ozren and seize control of the road between Mala Bukovica and Stanari, use some of the forces pursuant to a decision of the General Staff to contribute to the effort of lifting the siege of Sarajevo and the Podrinje area." You agree that the goals set in this directive for the 2nd and 3rd Corps is crystal clear, do you not? The goal being liberating the general Vozuca area and cutting off the Chetnik forces at Mount Ozren in order to be able to enlist the assistance of other corps to lift the siege of the Srebrenica and Zepa territories and get as far as Drina eventually? Would I be right in claiming that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For the purposes of the Trial Chamber, if you could just tell us this, the Srebrenica and Zepa areas, the Podrinje area, the Podrinje River Valley, those were protected UN areas, weren't they? Regardless of the protection they enjoyed, they faced an enormous amount of pressure from the Serb forces. Would I be right in stating that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this was the case in fact, yes. You are right, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. I see you have stopped because you're looking at us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, I thought you were about to ask the witness a question, and that's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- paused. May I press on now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. No, no. I do want to raise something with you that does concern me. I -- and before I ask the point or question, I just want to put it up front. I do understand that as a cross-examiner you are entitled to lead the witness, to put leading questions to the witness. I'm aware of that. But when you look at your question, if you look at that screen from page 13, line 4 up to page 14, line 4, that's you speaking and the witness says "yes," after all that long speech. And I ask myself, what is he saying yes to? And I ask myself, When -- when judgement is to be written, what -- what sense do we make out of that? I would prefer you to put a question and let the witness answer, even if you want a "yes" answer only. If you want a "yes" answer or a "no" answer, put as one fact at a time. Then we'll know exactly what we're talk -- what he's saying "yes" to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, well, I do understand what you are suggesting. I'm trying to ask short questions, but this was not a question. This was a quote. What I spent the last few minutes doing is quoting this particular directive. And my only question - perhaps it didn't come across as very clear - was a question that wasn't that long really, and I'm about to repeat it. I do understand the point you're trying to make, and I will try in the future to keep my questions as brief as possible and ask single questions and not multiple ones. I know exactly what you're saying, and thank you for this caution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. You're quoting something that we are going to ask that it be admitted into evidence, and if you go back to our guidelines, they say if you have quoted it as extensively as you have done, then it shouldn't be admitted because you're just burdening the record. But even then, you can ask the witness, because you have given him the copy of the document, to read it silently, put your question, and get an answer, but, you know, a short focused question which all of us can understand. That's all I'm asking for. Okay? But you say you understand. You may proceed, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's true, isn't it, that the goal of this directive was to lift the siege of free territories of Srebrenica and Zepa. Those areas were facing a horrendous situation, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one of the goals. That much is certain, yes. I think that paragraph 2 of the commander's decision states this, in no uncertain terms, what the goals were, to liberate the territories and to ease the pressure on the protected areas, the UN-protected areas. It also states the goal of setting free and using again roads, industrial facilities, getting them up and running, that sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree that these measures were necessary for the survival of thousands of people who were stuck in those areas that were under siege?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Supreme Command Staff envisaged a tragedy early 1995. They predicted that a disaster would occur, and this was one of the reasons for them issuing this directive. Would I be right in saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not exactly aware of what they were predicting at the time, but I think this directive was a result of assessments and predictions made not just by the Supreme Command Staff but also by the country's leaders. This is high politics. This is about negotiations. This is about agreements that were being reached. And we know that negotiations were very much futile at the time and continue to be that way all the way up until Dayton, to all practical intents. We know that many areas and enclaves were at risk. This also included the Bosanska Krajina area, the Sarajevo area itself, which was another UN-protected area, and all the other areas. Those most at risk, of course, were Zepa and Srebrenica, and we know what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that's where the disaster struck. Over a matter of days, over seven thousand people were killed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what most information seems to indicate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that this directive talked about certain assignments that were justified in the military sense and fully so?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was every military justification. I think it's an inalienable right of any ethnic group to try to protect itself and save itself from extinction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you about another aspect of the document now. Do you agree that a directive is a general document normally detailing general tasks and assignments to corps?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you've just said is something that has been bothering me for a long time, and during the war as well. It was a general document. Did it have to be like that? I don't know. We never really analysed what was done pursuant to this do you -- document. This is the most general kind of document in terms of its nature. This is a general plan, the most general plan possible on how to wage a war of liberation. Had we not carried this through in Vozuca -- well, we hadn't around Tesic and nobody was asking any questions, were they? In my opinion, the questions should have been asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But the point of my question is this: General Delic is not handing out any assignments to any particular unit in this directive apart from these general assignments in reference to the corps; right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, no particular tasks. These are very, very general sweeping assignments, very broad. They don't get any broader than this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can put this document away, but can it please be assigned a number before we do that. I'll come back to it at a later stage, but for the moment I want to move on to another document, P2423.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we give you an opportunity to assign it. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 384.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, this document is about to turn up. I wish to state for the record that this is a document by the 3rd Corps command dated the 22nd of August, 1995. This is an order, a stepping up combat readiness order. Witness, can you please have a look. It's a brief document.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm done.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that above all - at least, that's what the OTP told us - you studied this document closely while you were being prepped for your testimony here; right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the 22nd of August, 1995. That was the best look I got it at it, because I was the person who actually produced this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you agree, then, that there is an attachment to this document, a plan, the implementation of assignments given by the General Staff and measures to be taken by the 3rd Corps to step up combat readiness?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now turn the page. There's just one thing I'd like you to look at, sir. It's the -- the first box. It says that: "This order --" Oh, right. I apologise, Your Honours. All right. There you go. Number 1 in the English. The first box reads: "Develop plan 'Farz' and provide high degree of safety and success." You say that you were the person that produced this document, don't you. Now, you see that there's reference there to the Farz plan. I want to ask you something about this. This plan, Farz, is a plan of combat activities for the 3rd Corps in September 1995, is it not?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed it is. This is a plan that was devised by the 3rd Corps. This is what they called it. It was about lifting the siege of the Zavidovici-Tuzla road and also liberating the Vozuca pocket.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now move on to the following page, please, page 5 in the English. Page 5. Witness, right at the top of the page you see paragraph 9. Have a look, please, so I don't have to quote for the record. Can you look at paragraphs 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, and 16. It's just what I've been talking about, Your Honours. The pages 10, 11, 13, 14, and 16 are on the following pages. If we can get these pages on our screens, please, in English, the next page. And until such time, Witness, please try to comment on the other paragraphs there you can see. Do you agree that this implementation plan in paragraph 9 entailed assignments by the General Staff in terms of the responsibility of the command staff in terms of combat readiness and carrying out combat operations, and this is something that you included in your plan in relation to lower-ranking commands? Is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if the General Staff plan entailed this, but I do know that the General Staff knew about this too, and I did. So it was possible. I know that we needed to remain adamant about reinforcing the command and control structure in lower-ranking units, given the situation in terms of technical ability and -- and in training as well as the overall command and control situation that prevailed in lower-ranking units at the time. As for this assignment, I'm not sure if it stems from this particular plan, but I know that it was indispensable in terms of its inclusion in the 3rd Corps plan in relation to their subordinate units. The plan did entail a necessity to detect criminal activities under paragraph 11.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then under 13, direction of the General Staff to continue working on building the subordinate unit's morale. Did you instruct subordinate units to that effect?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This assignment was given to subordinate units' commands. There was the corps command handed down this instruction of the General Staff to re-study it with the purpose of building morale.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make an assessment of the vices and readiness of the command personnel?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you instructed them to analyse the work of court martial and responsibilities of commanders and other measures to be taken. That's under 16. And, Your Honours, that's on page 7 of the English version. I apologise. This is the following page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this task was assigned, because it was thought that it was necessary to do something in this respect in preparation and mobilisation of the people for the forthcoming combat operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the General Staff and the command of the 3rd Corps did much to build up the morale, to fight crime in the subordinate units? Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we admit this document into evidence and give it an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 385.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have the witness to take a look at document P2456. P2456. It is, for the benefit of the record, it is a decision of the General Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina dated 26th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this document. It is entitled "Undertaking of measures as per the directive for 1995." Do you agree that that directive is the one that we perused a couple of moments ago?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And could you tell me, please, that do you agree that this document was forwarded to the commands of the 2nd and 3rd Corps, personally to the commanders?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that it was produced at Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we scroll down, please, so that we can see the end of the document, both in the B/C/S and the English versions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It can be seen, do you agree with me, that -- yes, this is on that page in the English version. So, Witness, do you agree next to the rubber stamp there is the word "approved" and there is a signature?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, this is the signature of the chief of staff of the operational centre, Mr. Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall where he was located?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, he was at Kakanj together with the person who produced this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these initials indicate that --

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- do you agree that this document was not signed by General Delic?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it is not signed by him. We used to receive this document through packet service. Most probably Brigadier Dzambasovic approved the signals, personnel to relay it. But I know that this document or this order reached us after the planning had been finished, and I believe that the command -- corps command went to the forward command post at Luke.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I want to ask you about: Do you agree that the planning for the operation had complete -- been completed until the 26th of August, 1995, on the part of the both 3rd Corps and the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for the 3rd Corps that it had been completed. I think that the approval had been signed or the -- it -- the action was approved.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing I'd like to ask you is: Provided that General Delic was at Kakanj on that stage -- on that moment, there would be no reason for somebody else forwarding the document in his stead. He would have signed it were he there.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every soldier at the communications centre knew his signature and there would be no need for another approval.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about the nub of this document. Do you agree that by this document it was ordered from the command post for -- of Kakanj that commanders of the 2nd and 3rd Corps should prepare -- prepare and elaborate documents in relation to the liberation of the Vozuca pocket? Do you agree that this is stated in -- under 1, item 1 of the document?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is stated so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is also written that it should be sent back to Kakanj so that it could approve and regulate all the other matters concerning the implementation in order to approve all the other matters. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you another thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 386.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, regardless of who signed this document, General Jusic, please tell me, it is correct, is it not, that it is clearly visible that the General Staff hands down tasks to the commanders of the 2nd and 3rd Corps, their immediate subordinates? Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the procedure. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that's the procedure. The commander of the General Staff is not empowered to hand down directions to the second line of subordinate units; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, as a matter of principle, never issues orders to the 2nd or 3rd line of subordinate units, because in -- by doing so, he would be ignoring the existence and the functioning of the commands of the immediate subordinates. This would never happen, I think. I don't recall it ever happening during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, thank you. In other words, corps commander will decide and define the task of divisions and autonomous units of divisions.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. A corps commander defines the tasks to the divisions and brigades, but there were several immediately subordinate units such as the 3rd Sabotage Reconnaissance Detachment, battalion of military police, anti-aircraft units, and ABHO and communications company. These were subordinate units of -- smaller than battalions but as per our schematic, they were directly immediately subordinate to the corps command or the commander of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it was envisaged that they -- these units were organically within the composition of the corps.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Brigade commanders would then relay those tasks to their subordinate units, battalions, et cetera; am I right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Division commander to brigade commanders, and staff units; brigade commanders to their subordinate units, such as battalions and autonomous companies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to go back to -- to the Farz operation that we've been discussing. You told us that the commander could hand down a task or, alternatively, he could approve.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which commander? If I may interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I am talking about the commander of the Supreme Command Staff or General Staff, and you recently said that the commander could either approve a task from the immediate subordinate or hand down a task to the immediate subordinate.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So such approval would be given on maps when the commander would have available the graphical representations of the planned actions. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As per standards, commanders would approve activities and plans on a map. Mostly he would analyse maps. And in this concrete example, the whole plan was forwarded to the army staff, headed by General Hadzihasanovic. He analysed and studied that plan and proposed to the commander to approve it. I'm not sure how -- to which extent the commander would analyse and study that. I presume that he believed and trusted his chief of staff and his subordinates. I think even that I delivered it personally. And it seems to me that he signed it just taken a look -- having taken a look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going back to the plan. When you say "a complete plan" you mean the plan of the 3rd Corps and not of the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just the plan of the 3rd Corps. I reiterate.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are talking about the 3rd Corps' plan, not the plan for the subordinate units or lower units.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When a commander approves a plan on a map of the 3rd Corps or any other corps, he -- he does not hand down the tasks or he does not see the task of units which are below the level of corps. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would see only the tasks of the units which are directly subordinate to the corps command. Division command, autonomous units which are part of the corps command and brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you said when you delivered that plan to the General Staff, to Kakanj, you meant the plan that you had occasion to see yesterday.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. A complete plan was delivered to the army staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does this mean, "the complete plan," so that the Trial Chamber understands you?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The complete plan contains both the graphic outlay and the textual -- the text, the narrative, which means the text of the order for the operation. This is a document number 1 in that plan. Furthermore, the schematic of the decision and the plan on a map. Furthermore, orders for important activities, such as intelligence and reconnaissance, security, together with a plan of morale and political affairs in both text and in tables. Then an order for the artillery, together with the action plan that targets for the artillery. Then anti-aircraft defence, ABHO orders, and the plan and order for the communications. This would be a most complex plan, because it would elaborate into great detail how communications should be organised. This would be a very voluminous plan. And finally, a plan and an order of the assistant commander for logistics. All these plans and orders, the individual orders I listed, were signed by the commander and the plans attached to those orders and for the implementation of those orders were signed by the organs who produced them. Orders list the tasks for the immediately subordinate units. That would be the commander of the 35th Division, the commander of the 37th Division, 33rd, 14th Brigade, 7th Muslim Brigade, 375th Brigade, 1st and 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion, and the 3rd Sabotage and Reconnaissance Detachment. I think that security, morale, and political issues and logistics were also detailed out.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will revisit this part that you testified about to provide further clarifications, because I would like to ask you about, specifically about the situation on the unit that we mentioned yesterday. But before that, please, Witness, I would like you to see the map that we mentioned yesterday. I would like the witness to see it as well, because what we saw on the screen was very poorly visible. I would like the Chamber and the witness to see the map that we received. It is a photocopy of the original in colours, and we provided copies for the Trial Chamber, the learned friends, and the witness so that we can elicit some explanations from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, first of all I would like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But before that, Your Honours -- Witness, first of all, I would like you to confirm that this is the same map that you saw yesterday and that you drew lines on and encircled certain locations prompted by the Prosecutor. Could you confirm?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the same map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic, just before you proceed, do we have a copy for Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do. However, he signaled to us that he didn't need one, since we spent a long time studying this map together with General Delic, he knows it by heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I see him smiling and raising a hand. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, do you agree with me that it says "attack plan of the 3rd Corps between the 10th of September and the 10th of October"? Is that correct? I would like you to ask -- I would like to ask you to look at the bottom portion, what is relevant, and I will then go back to the upper part, where it says "approved army General Rasim Delic." It says here that he approved the map and the plan. Can you explain to us why there is no rubber stamp there. It would be customary to see one there, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There should be a rubber stamp here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us go to the lower portion of the map where we can see everything marked. Maybe we can put the map on the ELMO, but I believe that Your Honours can follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps at this moment I could kindly ask the witness to take the map with him during the break, to have a good look at it, and then we can go back to the map after the break, since I will have several questions concerning the map, if possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see Mr. Wood is on his feet. Yes, Mr. Wood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: Just a point of clarification, Your Honour. I see here, page 29, line 17, 18, 19, "It would be customary to see one there," referring to a rubber stamp. I just wonder, before we take the break, if he -- she could clarify -- Defence counsel can clarify with the witness exactly what she's talking about, whether where on the map there is no rubber stamp or appears to be none.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe you understood the question. I would like to thank my learned friend. It is important for us to clarify something. Can you see a stamp on this map and where should it be? Also, what sort of a stamp it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are now discussing the upper left corner. I believe that is what the Prosecutor had in mind.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part where there should be a signature and the stamp of the commander, we can see the signature but there is no stamp. I don't know why that is. There should be one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- can I just ask a question: Is there a signature of Mr. Delic on this map? I see his name. I don't see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The upper left corner, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm looking at the upper left corner. I see his name. I don't see his signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look, witness.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see his signature. That is his signature, just below "Rasim," it says "D." You can clearly make out "Rasim Delic" and then his signature, "D" and the rest of the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We do not dispute that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I thought that looks to me like part of the lines of the map. I -- I take --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're not disputing that, Your Honour, since the witness has already confirmed to us that he saw him sign that. It is a bit unclear, but one can say that that is indeed his signature. Perhaps we can continue discussing the map after the break. Does this suffice my learned friend, the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your learned friend the Prosecutor asked about the stamp and where it should be. If you can deal with that when we come back.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, can you tell us where it should be?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be across the signature. It should be a round large stamp of the General Staff, or below the signature. But at least part of the signature should be visible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I can see a stamp there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it seems to me that one can make out the stamp as well. But at the moment I was putting the question, I wasn't able to see that. However, the copy that you have is of better quality than the one I have that was given to us by the Prosecutor. I believe there is a stamp there. Perhaps the witness can confirm that. We are not disputing in any way, Your Honour, that General Delic indeed signed the map. I just wanted to know why there is no stamp.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are correct. There is a stamp there to the left of the letter "R." That is the stamp. I know its size, and this is the proper place for it, so that it partially covers the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour, we are not disputing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would this then be an appropriate moment? We'll take a break and come back at 4.00, Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe you had sufficient time to have a good look at the map, the map of the Farz plan.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know -- I've known it since 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the -- the key, which is in the lower left corner, I believe. It says "Key." There are four arrows, as far as I can understand. They are also in different colours. Is it correct that they should depict the tasks of the 2nd and 3rd Corps? Am I understanding it correctly?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the main role of the arrows. However, they should also indicate the direction of activities or operations. They also differ in terms of colour. Therefore, the arrows' role is twofold: The direction of movement of units, and how far they should go in performing the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, those are the tasks of the unit.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that we can see here the tasks of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the tasks of units immediately subordinated to the 3rd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear you, Madam Vidovic, and the witness seem to see the tasks of the corps and see the significance of those arrows. I for one, I don't see -- I don't understand anything, if you're saying the arrows show the direction of movement, if you say they are different colours, I want to know what is the significance of the difference in colours, and what the tasks are that are being mentioned in each arrow. One, I don't understand the language. Two, even if I did, I don't think I'd be able to understand what the tasks are just by looking at the arrow and the -- and the words next to the arrow. And then I wouldn't understand the significance of the difference in colours. So as you go along and agree with each other, take us along. Tell us what the colour means, what is the direction of each one, which one is 3rd Corps instruction there. I see 2nd Corps and the other one is zadatak and it's detailed twice. I don't see 3rd Corps there, so please help us understand. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us look at the key again.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under the word "key," is there a light yellow arrow? It says "immediate task."

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Below that, there is a dark yellow arrow and the words there are "following," "the following task."

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was supposed to be the following task.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Perhaps in practice it should have been the following task, but now we can only discuss what we can see on the map. The second arrow and the words after it read "the following task"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Underneath there, the third arrow says "subsequent task." Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the pink or light purple arrow reads "2nd Corps task"; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If we have a look at another portion of the map, on the opposite side, can you explain to the Chamber that what we see here are certain directions marked with arrows bearing different colours? Can you explain that to us? You took part in the planning. Can you tell us whether indeed we can see different colours on the map and what they mean.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By your leave, certainly I will explain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the key on the map is an explanation of certain markings or a part of the plan that we can see depicted on the map. The arrows were there to show -- for example, let's have a look at the Vozuca pocket. From the west to the east, we see yellow arrows. And at the tip of those arrows, there is a dotted line connecting all of the yellow arrows. Please have a look at this part, where it says -- where it says "the 7th Muslim Brigade," looking from the west towards the east. At the top of the -- at the tip of those arrows, you can see a dotted blue line, and it depicts the immediate task to be performed by these units. That was the line in the field which they were supposed to reach in the course of the immediate task. The following task is the advancement of units. And that is standard procedure to call tasks immediate, following, and subsequent. The next phase, as explained already by the Defence counsel, is marked in darker yellow, and the tips of the arrows are connected by a double dotted line. That was the area in the field that the units were supposed to reach in the following task. The green arrows depict the subsequent task and the line to be reached in the course of that task. For the 3rd Corps, it was the River Krivaja. We have a double dotted line interspersed with the dots. That was supposed to be the subsequent task. This was the subsequent task for the 3rd Corps; whereas, the 2nd Corps had their subsequent task to reach the Krivaja River from the opposite side. We can see their arrows here, pertaining to the 2nd Corps. The map depicts the axis of activity of the 2nd Corps, and the tips of the arrows show the area which they were supposed to reach. The line of contact is the double dotted line interspersed with dots. Can you follow me, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not quite. I see you pointing at arrows which seem to be coming from the north-west towards the double dotted line, which I would have assumed would have been the task of the -- of the 3rd Corps, because the -- the 2nd Corps, I thought, should be coming from east going west. That's how I thought it should be. And I see one, two, three arrows that show the movement of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. That is what I wanted to explain. I described the immediate, following, and subsequent tasks of the 3rd Corps; that is, my corps. I wanted to explain what the colours mean, as well as the arrows that we can see in the key and what they are supposed to represent on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just follow up with one question to the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: double tracked. Does that have any significance or is it just to show that this is the following attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct. It merely indicates that it is the next task of the same unit, of the same force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So it has nothing to do with the speed of the advance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you told us that you are very familiar with the map, and now you had an occasion to see it again. A simple question therefor: Would you with me that there are no tasks depicted on this map that would pertain to the El Mujahidin unit? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this map, we can see the tasks of the 35th Division, then of the 7th Muslim Brigade, the 375th Brigade, and the 1st Manoeuvre Battalion as units who are immediately subordinated to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question therefore is: Can you confirm to us that we do not see the tasks of the El Mujahidin unit on the map?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume that the order of the 3rd Corps did not envisage any particular movements of the El Mujahidin detachment. However, in the 35th Division, they had their own tasks, and their tasks are depicted on the map, and they, the El Mujahidin Detachment, were a part of the 35th Division. Therefore their tasks should be encompassed in the tasks of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But can you see that on the map? That is the question.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is difficult to answer the way you want me to. I know where the unit went; however, it is not marked on the map. We do not see its first and last name on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this was for the reason that it needn't be marked on the map? Or, rather, can you explain to the Chamber - I don't want to lead. I want to elicit answers from you - do you know why we cannot see the unit on the map?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot see any particular unit of the 35th Division at the level of battalion. Therefore, standard procedure does not require to depict units of subordinate commands. Therefore, we do not see them here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is because that unit is at least three levels down below the General Staff, which was supposed to approve this attack. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The General Staff would be the fourth level up.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore the General Staff would be four levels up, compared to the El Mujahidin Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning this, I want to ask you the following: Is this correct, is it not, that General Delic by signing approved the plan of activities of the 3rd Corps, and they approved their task as his immediately subordinated unit? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that General Delic, or rather, the General Staff, approved the plan for the 3rd Corps, including only the subordinated units of the 3rd Corps -- the first subordinated units of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore that does not encompass the El Mujahidin detachment?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mujahidin detachment was not part of the 3rd Corps. Several months before that it had been resubordinated to the command of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this map as an exhibit since I believe it is much clearer and easier to understand and therefore will be of greater assistance to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 387.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But before we leave the map, Mrs. Vidovic, I think it would be useful if the general could assist us in pointing out some of the locations which we were discussing yesterday and which brought us to an exchange of views about the -- the -- the accuracy of the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: My question is: If we look right north from Paljenik, we see a flag saying "34" -- sorry, "35" and then IKM, and that is Livarde. I suppose that was the forward command post of the 35th Division at Livarde; is that correct, General?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of the 35th Division at Livarde. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then if we move down towards the south from that point, it says in the middle of the area 35D and then KOV. What does that mean? Is that just the area of responsibility of the 35th Division or ...? Do you see it? Yes, there, just where you have your pen. There.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the name of the 35th Division of the land forces. This is the mark inscribed by the map writer and should be in the middle of the zone of responsibility of that division. We have discussed this, division zone of responsibility from Krvavac and north of Maglaj. In my opinion, it would have been better if that mark were made here with larger -- in larger letters, larger letters than the letters for the brigades. And this would be as -- as per our standards. But whoever drew this map, they did it poorly. They should have relocated the marking, because then one would be misled to believing that this is -- only this was the responsibility of the 35th Division. But this whole area was their zone of responsibility. This is not a zone. This is the name of the largest unit whose zone of responsibility this is, and this is the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. And the reason I'm asking, of course, is that if you look south of Zavidovici, there you see again the same marking of the 35th Division in -- in larger letters now. So I just wanted to be sure if there was any difference between the two, but I understand from your testimony that the whole -- the whole operation was controlled by the 35th Division. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No. Oh.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The operation was managed by the commander of the 3rd Corps, Your Honours. This is the overall zone. But in this region, we had defensive units which were under the 35th Division. So they were engaged in defence. But the other units were encompassed by this plan and the plan envisaged their engagement in defence. But the basis and the launch pad for the offensive part of the operation were units outside the 35th Division, because the 35th Division was involved through one or two battalions. Most of those attacking units were from the 3rd Corps: The 7th Muslim, 375th Brigade, 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Manoeuvre Battalions, sabotage and reconnaissance companies. All these units were part of the command of the 3rd Corps. They were subordinated immediately to them. And in practical terms, the Operation Farz was commanded by the 3rd Corps command and was effected in the area where the 35th Division had organized and maintained defence for years before that in 1992, 1993, 1994, and then in 1995. If you have not grasped what I am saying, you may ask additional questions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand you perfectly well, but I just wanted it to be clear, because I saw that the -- these markings had been done several places on the map. Thank you. So one more question: Also on the map, inside the pocket you see small signs of armoury or weaponry in red. I would assume that these are the Serb -- or the -- the Serbian positions? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are Serb -- Serb positions marked in red.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe -- let me also just raise one or two questions. At coordinate longitude 14 and vertical 20, there -- there's a name there, "7.vmobr." What does that mean? Longitudinal 14 and latitudinal 20. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have. This is the 7th -- the 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade. And you have the digits "7" and "10" behind it in red. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which means -- this is the name of the 7th Muslim Brigade. It had its full title as follows: It was the Chivalrous -- 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade. And this is the area where they were located and performed an attack, and that brigade, the 7th Chivalrous Muslim Liberation Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. Then at coordinate longitudinal 10 and latitudinal 24, there's a little fleck there to the left, and below it in a -- in a south-easterly direction there's 1.mnb. What does that stand for?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The acronym -- the acronym for the 1st Manoeuvre Battalion, which was directly subordinated to the command of the 3rd Corps, which means it was immediately subordinated unit, and manoeuvre battalions were immediately subordinated units of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And finally, we -- we have Exhibit 380, which was this map that was being used, I think, by the OPT yesterday -- OTP, I beg your pardon. Notwithstanding that, you still want this one to go in? I understand that that one was not as detailed as this one. It was much smaller and...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, yes, Your Honour. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And we have given it Exhibit number 387. Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may continue, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may. You may. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to dwell on planning a while longer. Did I understand you correctly when you said that in July 1995 the Vozuca action was not planned by the 3rd Corps but, rather, by the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me correctly. At that point -- at that time, the 3rd Corps command was engaged in the lifting of the siege of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which means that this plan was approved by the corps command, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must explain this right now. I did not see that plan at all, but I think I did not see it and I don't know whether the commander signed it, but I think he did, because that activity would not have been implemented without his signature. It was not submitted for study. I did not study it, but I think the commander approved it. I stress, after explaining the difference between "approved" or"authorised" and "given" or "received" tasks, I think that the commander approved it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Which means that the plan for the July action was not approved by the Supreme Command Staff. Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That plan did not go to the -- through the approval procedure at the Supreme Command Staff as per our standards. Such plans approved by 3rd Corps or corps level should not or do not have to be relayed upwards to Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that you were involved in Operation Farz planning, and you told us at the time the El Mujahid division was resubordinated to the 35th Division. Am I right in concluding that neither in the written decisions and orders nor in the maps and plans the El Mujahedin was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct. That detachment, that unit was not mentioned anywhere there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, in the plan that was seen by the staff, be it by General Delic or General Hadzihasanovic, there was no mention of the El Mujahedin detachment. No, there was no markings and no mention, and they could not know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll ask you another question about this thing. Do you agree that units which are attached to some other units or are resubordinated to some other units, that they are given the tasks by the commander in whose composition that unit implements a combat task? Am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. By all means, the resubordinated unit must effect the orders of the commander to whom they're resubordinated, and that command is duty-bound to supply them with everything as if they were their own unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Discussing the issue of commanding yesterday, you said, and you reiterated that today that, the July operation against the Vozuca pocket was commanded by the -- a commander of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you said that the September operation was commanded from one axis -- from one direction by the 3rd Corps and from the other direction, the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, commander of the 2nd Corps from one direction and the commander of the 3rd Corps from the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to focus on the September operation, and in connection with that, I would like to have the witness see the document D390. And for the record, before it appears on the screen, I would like to say that this is an information of the forward command post of the 3rd Corps at Luke dated 29th of August, 1995. Let us see whether it's on the screen in both versions. And would the witness please peruse this document. You said yesterday that the 3rd Corps established a forward command post for that September operation at Luke and Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Luke, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So did I understand you correctly that this was the forward command post from which combat activities were commanded from on the part of the 3rd Corps against the Vozuca pocket?

utterances.speaker: KADIR JUSIC [Resumed]
